travels with the cancellation so the resulting `TurnCancelled` can say
which one it was, and a consumer that reads only the event still knows
whether the run ended.

ToolFailure.description:
**Why a tool call did not work**, classified by the adapter from the
structured fields it already reads.

Five classes and no sixth escape hatch that carries text. A provider
that failed a call in a way the adapter cannot place is
[`Unclassified`](Self::Unclassified) — which is a fact worth showing
("it failed, and the provider did not say how") and is never a guess.

oneOf.description: It was not allowed to run — an approval refused, a permission denied.
It was stopped before it finished.
It ran out of time.
It ran and reported an error.

It did not succeed, and the provider did not say why in a way this
adapter can place.

ToolKind.description:

vocabulary onto this list, and a tool it has no token for is

text.

AgentEvent.description:
Provider-neutral managed-session facts. Provider IDs and native wire values
never cross this boundary.

input.description:
Protocol v17 (UC17). What the agent asked the tool to do, as the
adapter read it from the call — a command line, the paths of a
change, an MCP tool's arguments — bounded to
[`TOOL_CONTENT_CHARS`]. `None` when the provider gave none, and
from an older peer.

detail.description:
Protocol v17. The tool's own account of why it failed, as the
provider reported it, bounded to [`TOOL_DETAIL_CHARS`]
characters — the first thing a person asks of a failed row, and
the one piece of provider text that crosses here. `None` when it
succeeded, when the provider said nothing readable, and from an
older peer. Never the arguments, never the results.

failure.description:
Protocol v14. Why it did not work, as the adapter classified it
from the structured fields it already reads — never the
provider's error text, which does not cross this boundary at
all. `None` when it succeeded, and `None` from an older peer,
which the run reads as [`ToolFailure::Unclassified`].

output.description:
Protocol v17 (UC17). What the tool produced, as the adapter read
it — a command's output, a change's diff, an MCP result — bounded
to [`TOOL_CONTENT_CHARS`]. `None` when the provider gave none,
and from an older peer.

tool.description:
Protocol v14. Which tool it was, as the adapter classifies it —
never the provider's own name for it. Absent from an older peer,
which reads as `None`: unknown, never guessed.

reason.description:
Protocol v14. Why the turn was cancelled. A peer that predates the
field reads `Run`, which is what every cancellation meant before
a takeover could end a step without ending the job.

oneOf.description:
Protocol v19 (koru-ai D7). The agent moved its approval mode itself
during the turn — Claude leaving plan mode once a plan is approved,
or taking another mode when the one asked for is not offered by its
model. A new tag, so the host sends it only to a v19 peer.

CatalogEvent.description:
The named catalog subscription's payload.

This stream is invalidation, never content and never a command: a holder
re-reads `ListProjects` at its own pace. Because every notification says
the same thing, a queue that is already full may drop one without a reader
missing anything — which is what makes the stream bounded by construction.

It is an enum with one arm rather than a bare struct so the next catalog
fact is a new variant instead of a second subscription.
CatalogEvent.title: CatalogEvent

ClientRole.description:
What a connection says it is in its hello. Absent is an ordinary
client; `AiControl` is the AI worker's one control connection, and is
what a chat-origin create needs to be admitted.
ClientRole.title: ClientRole

ControlRequestOutcome.description: The answer to a control request.

oneOf.description: No controller is held: attach now.

A controller is held and has been told. The requester waits for the
session's handover to read `Released`, then attaches.

ControlRequestOutcome.title: ControlRequestOutcome

ErrorCode.description: Stable error token; unknown values remain errors.

HandoverState.description:
Where a controller handover stands.

Release, not preemption: nothing takes a lease from its holder. The
holder is asked, releases at a boundary of its choosing, the requester
attaches, and gives it back the same way. Each step is a state a reader
can see and an event a subscriber receives.

oneOf.description: Someone asked while a controller was held; the holder has been told.

The holder released its lease for the handover; the next attach takes
it.
The lease was granted after a release: a person holds the session.
The person gave the lease back, or lost it; the next attach reclaims.

ModelIdentity.description:
The model a session asked for and the model the provider says it used.

They differ — a provider may reroute — and a provider may say nothing,
which is an explicit `None` rather than a copy of the request. Pricing
needs the reported one; a comparison across runs needs both.

the bus carries an `Id` reference to retained metadata instead (§17.3).

ProviderKind.description: Provider category, never a provider-native identity.

SessionFailure.description: A content-free developer diagnostic. UI maps `code` to localized copy.

SessionOrigin.description:
What created a session. Defaulted to `Manual` on every peer that
predates it, which is the truth: before v16 only windows created
sessions without a delegation launch.

SessionProfileKey.description:
Stable identity for a launch profile. Built-ins remain readable across
machines; user-created profiles are opaque UUIDs.

handover.description:
Protocol v14. Where a controller handover stands. `Idle` from a peer
that predates handovers, which is the truth on a host that has none.

model.description:
Protocol v14. The model the session asked for and the one last
reported, for a managed session whose adapter can say. `None` from a
raw session, an older peer, or an adapter that reports neither.

origin.description:
Protocol v16. What created this session. `Manual` from a peer that
predates origins, which is the truth for every session a window made.
A chat's session is never drawn by a window, a tray or a flyout: its
chat is its view.

project_id.description:
The project this session was placed in, if any. Absent from a peer
that predates projects, which is why it defaults rather than being
required; absent for a session nobody placed, which the tree draws
under its virtual Unassigned bucket rather than a persisted project.

CreationLookup.description:
The answer to a non-creating lookup of a creation key.

Retrying `create_profile_session` is not a safe way to ask "did it
start?": on a missing key the host falls through and spawns. This is the
question asked as a question. It never creates, never retires, and never
takes a lease — and it is paired with the host's `instance_id`, because
"no evidence" from the same host incarnation and "no evidence" from a
restarted one are different facts.

oneOf.description: A live session carries the key: it started and is running.

The key is reserved and insertion has not completed: a process may
exist right now. Never the nothing-running branch.

No live session, but the host retained the creation's outcome: it
started and has finished.

Nothing under this key. With a new `instance_id` the host restarted
and nothing survived; with the same one, nothing is running.

CreationLookup.title: CreationLookup

McpBearer.description:
The bearer a delegated provider presents at its MCP endpoint.

The run authority's endpoint token (`koru_run_…`, ADR-348), issued once
per attempt and rotated when the generation advances. Bounded and opaque
the way [`McpEndpoint`] is, and redacted from `Debug` — but held to a
stricter rule than the endpoint: **it is never rendered anywhere a
second process can read it.** An adapter puts it in the child's own
environment, never on argv, which every process on the machine can see,
and never in a file it leaves behind (ADR-359).

McpEndpoint.description:
Where a delegated provider reaches Koru's MCP tools.

An `http://` or `https://` URL the adapter renders privately into the
provider's own configuration form. It names a run's endpoint, so it is
redacted from `Debug` the way a lease token is: an id in a URL is still
an id somebody could replay. Neither quote character is allowed, so an
adapter can embed it in any configuration syntax without escaping.

McpToolAllowlist.description:
The bounded, duplicate-free set of tools one delegated launch allows.
Empty allows none, which is a legal launch: a run may be read-only.

McpToolName.description:
One MCP tool name a delegated provider may call: lowercase, digits and
underscores, as MCP tools are spelled.

ModelName.description:
A provider's model name, as the provider spells it.

Bounded and printable, and otherwise opaque: Koru compares it, stores it
beside a run's economics and prices it at display, but never interprets
it. It is not an event attribute — `AttrValue` has no free string, and
the bus carries an `Id` reference to retained metadata instead (§17.3).

ProviderResumeToken.description:
An adapter's opaque handle for resuming a provider session it once ran.

Bounded and never printed. Koru stores it beside a run's attempt and
hands it back unchanged; only the adapter that minted it can read it,
and an adapter that declares no native resume never mints one.

DelegationLaunch.description:
What a delegated launch hands the adapter beyond the profile: the MCP
endpoint it must render, the bearer that authenticates this attempt
there, the tools it may allow, and the resume token of the attempt it
continues, if any.

Its presence on a creation is what makes the creation a delegation. A
host that did not negotiate `delegation` refuses it rather than spawning
a provider that would never reach its tools.

credential.description:
The endpoint's bearer. Defaulted, so a peer that predates it reads
the message: `None` is a launch whose endpoint refuses every call,
which is what a host without a run authority could ever have offered
anyway.

model.description: Explicit requested model; absent preserves the provider's own default.

Bounded and printable, and otherwise opaque: Koru compares it, stores it
beside a run's economics and prices it at display, but never interprets
it. It is not an event attribute — `AttrValue` has no free string, and
the bus carries an `Id` reference to retained metadata instead (§17.3).

session is started with; the id is the agent's, opaque to Koru.

OriginLookup.description:
The answer to `lookup_origin`: what the registry holds under an origin

that finds nothing live and nothing reserved may create, and admission
is what makes that race-free.

WorkspaceScope.description:
The Koru catalog place one project belongs to.

A typed pair, versioned with the protocol, rather than a compound string:
opaque to the session host does not mean unstructured on the wire. A

ProjectSummary.description:
One project row. There is deliberately no `sort_key` and no lifecycle
field: archiving a workspace hides its projects without mutating any of
them, so there is nothing here for an `ArchiveProject` verb to write.

root_directory.description:
An absolute local path chosen by the user, or none until "Set folder…"
supplies one. A project with no root launches from today's default; a
project whose root has gone missing refuses to launch instead of
silently falling back.

Provider-neutral managed-session facts. Provider IDs and native wire values

input.description:
Protocol v17 (UC17). What the agent asked the tool to do, as the
adapter read it from the call — a command line, the paths of a
change, an MCP tool's arguments — bounded to
[`TOOL_CONTENT_CHARS`]. `None` when the provider gave none, and
from an older peer.

detail.description:
Protocol v17. The tool's own account of why it failed, as the
provider reported it, bounded to [`TOOL_DETAIL_CHARS`]
characters — the first thing a person asks of a failed row, and
the one piece of provider text that crosses here. `None` when it
succeeded, when the provider said nothing readable, and from an
older peer. Never the arguments, never the results.

failure.description:
Protocol v14. Why it did not work, as the adapter classified it
from the structured fields it already reads — never the
provider's error text, which does not cross this boundary at
all. `None` when it succeeded, and `None` from an older peer,
which the run reads as [`ToolFailure::Unclassified`].

output.description:
Protocol v17 (UC17). What the tool produced, as the adapter read
it — a command's output, a change's diff, an MCP result — bounded
to [`TOOL_CONTENT_CHARS`]. `None` when the provider gave none,
and from an older peer.

tool.description:
Protocol v14. Which tool it was, as the adapter classifies it —
never the provider's own name for it. Absent from an older peer,
which reads as `None`: unknown, never guessed.

reason.description:
Protocol v14. Why the turn was cancelled. A peer that predates the
field reads `Run`, which is what every cancellation meant before
a takeover could end a step without ending the job.

oneOf.description:
Protocol v19 (koru-ai D7). The agent moved its approval mode itself
during the turn — Claude leaving plan mode once a plan is approved,
or taking another mode when the one asked for is not offered by its
model. A new tag, so the host sends it only to a v19 peer.

AgentModeId.description:
One agent's own id for one of its modes: printable ASCII with no space,
at most [`MAX_AGENT_MODE_ID_BYTES`].

AgentUsage.description:
One usage report for one turn.

**The report is the total for `turn_id` so far, and a later report for
the same turn replaces the earlier one.** Whether the provider sends
deltas, running totals or replacements is the adapter's business to
declare in its compatibility note and normalize here; above this type
there is one total per turn. A missing count is `None` — unavailable is
never zero.

cached_input.description:
Protocol v14. How `cached_input_tokens` relates to `input_tokens`,
as the adapter declared it. Absent from an older peer, which reads as
`Undeclared` — incomplete, never guessed.

model.description:
Protocol v14. The model the provider reported for this turn, or
`None` when it said nothing. Never a copy of the model that was asked
for: that lives on the session summary as `requested`.

ApprovalChoice.description: Label is approval content, drawn but never included in diagnostics.

ApprovalIntent.description: Semantic intent; provider option identifiers never cross this boundary.

CachedInputRelationship.description:
Whether a provider's `input_tokens` already counts its cached input.

Declared by the adapter, never assumed: a wrong guess here misprices
every run silently. `Undeclared` is recorded as incomplete downstream,
which is the honest answer when the provider's note has not said.

oneOf.description: `cached_input_tokens` is a subset of `input_tokens`.
`cached_input_tokens` is counted beside `input_tokens`, not inside it.
The adapter has not said. Recorded incomplete, never guessed.

CancelReason.description:
Why a managed turn is being cancelled.

A takeover cancellation ends the step, not the job (D36). The reason
travels with the cancellation so the resulting `TurnCancelled` can say
which one it was, and a consumer that reads only the event still knows
whether the run ended.

oneOf.description: The run itself is being cancelled: terminal for the run.
The turn ends so control can be handed over: never terminal.

ToolFailure.description:
**Why a tool call did not work**, classified by the adapter from the
structured fields it already reads.

Five classes and no sixth escape hatch that carries text. A provider
that failed a call in a way the adapter cannot place is
[`Unclassified`](Self::Unclassified) — which is a fact worth showing
("it failed, and the provider did not say how") and is never a guess.

oneOf.description: It was not allowed to run — an approval refused, a permission denied.
It was stopped before it finished.
It ran out of time.
It ran and reported an error.

It did not succeed, and the provider did not say why in a way this
adapter can place.

ToolKind.description:
**Which tool ran**, as the adapter that watched it declares.

Not the provider's name for it: an adapter maps its provider's own tool
vocabulary onto this list, and a tool it has no token for is
[`Other`](Self::Other) — named as unknown rather than passed through as
text.

oneOf.description: Running a command.
Editing files.
A tool an MCP server offers.
A tool the provider loaded at runtime.

A tool this build has no token for. The honest answer when an
adapter — or an older peer that sent no kind at all — did not say.

Protocol v14. Where a controller handover stands. `Idle` from a peer
that predates handovers, which is the truth on a host that has none.

model.description:
Protocol v14. The model the session asked for and the one last
reported, for a managed session whose adapter can say. `None` from a
raw session, an older peer, or an adapter that reports neither.

origin.description:
Protocol v16. What created this session. `Manual` from a peer that
predates origins, which is the truth for every session a window made.
A chat's session is never drawn by a window, a tray or a flyout: its
chat is its view.

project_id.description:
The project this session was placed in, if any. Absent from a peer
that predates projects, which is why it defaults rather than being
required; absent for a session nobody placed, which the tree draws
under its virtual Unassigned bucket rather than a persisted project.

ShellQuoting.description:
The parser that will consume a quoted attachment path. This is profile
data, never inferred from an executable name.
ShellQuoting.title: ShellQuoting

TakeoverUrgency.description: How soon a control request wants the lease.

oneOf.description: Wait for the holder to release at the turn boundary.

Cancel the active turn with [`CancelReason::TakeoverBoundary`] so the
boundary arrives now. Still one rule: the request waits for the
boundary; this only brings the boundary forward.

TakeoverUrgency.title: TakeoverUrgency

text.description: One grapheme or an empty string for a wide-cell continuation.

mouse_reporting.description:
Compatibility summary retained for existing clients. New input paths
use `mouse_tracking` and `mouse_encoding` below.

TerminalMouseEvent.description:
One mouse report in zero-based active-grid coordinates.

The runtime combines this provider-neutral record with the emulator's live
negotiated tracking and encoding modes. A move with no button represents
all-motion reporting; drag moves retain their pressed button.
TerminalMouseEvent.title: TerminalMouseEvent

text.description: One grapheme or an empty string for a wide-cell continuation.

index.description: Stable retained-row coordinate, never an emulator-relative line index.

wrapped_to_next.description: The terminal's logical line continues directly into the next grid row.

ToolFailure.description:
**Why a tool call did not work**, classified by the adapter from the
structured fields it already reads.

Five classes and no sixth escape hatch that carries text. A provider
that failed a call in a way the adapter cannot place is
[`Unclassified`](Self::Unclassified) — which is a fact worth showing
("it failed, and the provider did not say how") and is never a guess.

oneOf.description: It was not allowed to run — an approval refused, a permission denied.
It was stopped before it finished.
It ran out of time.
It ran and reported an error.

It did not succeed, and the provider did not say why in a way this
adapter can place.

ToolFailure.title: ToolFailure

ToolKind.description:
**Which tool ran**, as the adapter that watched it declares.

Not the provider's name for it: an adapter maps its provider's own tool
vocabulary onto this list, and a tool it has no token for is
[`Other`](Self::Other) — named as unknown rather than passed through as
text.

oneOf.description: Running a command.
Editing files.
A tool an MCP server offers.
A tool the provider loaded at runtime.

A tool this build has no token for. The honest answer when an
adapter — or an older peer that sent no kind at all — did not say.

ToolKind.title: ToolKind

WorkspaceScope.description:
The Koru catalog place one project belongs to.

A typed pair, versioned with the protocol, rather than a compound string:
opaque to the session host does not mean unstructured on the wire. A
project with no scope belongs to no workspace and is visible everywhere.
WorkspaceScope.title: WorkspaceScope
